name: division_seeding_regimes
title: Division-threshold population regimes
claim: Raising the division mass threshold monotonically shrinks the final particle population in the full COMETS composite — a division-controlled population-size phase relationship.

purpose.question: How does the particle population size depend on the division mass threshold in the coupled field+agent COMETS composite?
purpose.mechanism: Parameter-sweep phase-diagram study (discovery engine): a real composite swept over one axis, reduced to a regime metric.
purpose.expected_outcome: The metric varies monotonically across the swept axis, revealing the regime relationship.

question: How does the particle population size depend on the division mass threshold in the coupled field+agent COMETS composite?

behavior_tests.name: DIVISION-SEEDING-POPULATION-DECREASES
behavior_tests.description: final particle population decreases monotonically as the division mass threshold rises.

DIVISION-SEEDING-POPULATION-DECREASES.detail: decreasing; steps [-19.33,-3.333]; net -30.67; start 69 end 38.33; tol 0.01

findings.statement: Averaged over 3 seeds, the final population falls monotonically across division thresholds 2->8 (69->38): a higher mass bar for division yields fewer, larger cells. Single seeds are noisy (the regime only emerges on the seed average), so this is a multiseed-robust population phase relationship.

resolved: Final population size is set monotonically by the division mass threshold.
remaining: The joint threshold x seeding-rate (add_rate) regime map is only sampled on one axis.

followup_study_proposals.motivation: A 2D sweep over division_mass_threshold x add_rate would map the full population phase diagram, not just the threshold axis.

falsifiability: If the seed-averaged final population did not fall as the division mass threshold rose, the division-controlled-population claim would be false.
limitations: One sweep axis (threshold) at fixed seeding rate; 3 seeds; a single horizon.
Single-seed runs are noisy — the regime is only robust on the seed average.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The population trend is driven by the seeding rate, not the division threshold.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: add_rate is held fixed across the sweep; only division_mass_threshold varies.
